newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria invites foreign observers to monitor poll.
newsitem.headline: Algeria invites foreign observers to monitor poll.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Thursday asked in letters the United Nations, the Arab League and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) to dispatch observers to supervise general elections in his troubled country.

"Algeria intends, through this gesture, to underline the particular interest which it holds to the success of the next parliamentary elections," Zeroual said in his letter reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.

Zeroual has promised to arrange parliamentary polls in the first half of this year and announced he would hold talks with legal opposition parties next week over setting up an independent committee to oversee the elections.
Algeria has been without parliament since January 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
The annulment of Algeria's first multiparty parliamentary poll plunged the North African country into five years of ruthless violence in which about 60,000 people have died.
Officials said the now outlawed FIS would be barred from fielding candidates in the election.
About 150 observers from the United Nations, OAU and Arab League monitored Algeria's presidential election in 1995.
